mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% signals tight monetary policy, increasing discount rates for equity valuation and reducing corporate borrowing capacity, which produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 4.0% signals monetary easing, lowering discount rates and boosting equity valuations, which produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate below 4.0% and unemployment rate below 4.0% signals coordinated monetary and labor market easing, reducing financing costs and increasing consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0% AND UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-crisis recovery phase, a rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1330 indicates improving consumer confidence and construction activity, fueling corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during the post-crisis recovery phase.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% (falling >0.2pp in 3 months) signals improving labor market conditions, increasing consumer spending and corporate profits, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) above 102.0 (rising >0.5% in 1 month) indicates robust manufacturing output, signaling strong economic activity and corporate earnings growth, which leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO rises > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate below 4.0% and rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1330 (rising >0.5% in 1 month) signals coordinated monetary easing and housing market recovery, reducing financing costs and boosting consumer confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.0% AND HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0% AND HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 311.0 (rising >0.5% in 1 month) signals inflationary pressure, which may trigger monetary tightening and increase discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month.
